svg.text: talk.01 · v0.5 study · HOW THE FOUR MODES SHOW, AND HOW THE WHEEL SENSES THEM
the owner's question: how to read 'which mode' from a wheel, arc or row, and is there a 4-position encoder
TENTATIVE · NOT A FINAL DESIGN
A ARC
The icons sit on an arc round the wheel; the
wheel's notch points at one.
The most honest picture of a rotary switch; one
glance, no learning. Needs a 30 mm arc of free
face, close to the cable and the wordmark.
B LEADERS
Ticks on the pocket, folded lines down to a row of
icons and names.
Neat and flexible: the row can sit anywhere. The
lines take about 24 x 12 mm and must be drawn
without crossing; the staircase here does not
cross.
C LIST
The same ticks, straight lines fanning out to a
short vertical list.
Reads like a legend, with names. Takes the most
width; the list shares the space of the wordmark.
D DIAL
The icons ride ON the wheel; a fixed triangle on
the body marks the active one (a camera mode
dial).
The smallest and the surest: the mode sits right
at your thumb, nothing else on the face. But the
icons are 2 mm, so a decal or a UV print.
Recommendation (a proposal): D, the dial, as the default, with A as a printed backup on a lid; B and C only if the face has room.
HOW TO SENSE FOUR POSITIONS (the thing that decides what the firmware can know)
1 encoder + detent
relative
An EC11-class incremental encoder (Alps EC11 comes with 12 to 36 detents and several shaft lengths; the body drawing must be checked). Cheap and
common. BUT it is relative: after a reset the firmware does not know where the wheel is. Fix: hard end stops plus a home switch at one end.
2 two switches + printed cam
absolute
A cam on the wheel presses two small switches in a Gray-code pattern: 00, 01, 11, 10 = four positions. Two GPIO pins, no special part, the position is
known at power-up. The detent is a spring ball or a printed flexure.
3 magnet + AS5600
absolute
A diametric magnet on the wheel axis over an AS5600 (12-bit, I2C, about 1 deg linearity; the datasheet asks for at least 8 mT). Any number of
positions, and later a volume use. More parts; the magnet must be placed over the chip.
4 potentiometer + ADC
absolute
Four voltage zones on one analog pin. Simple wiring, but the track wears and the zones drift; the detent is separate.
5 a ready 4-position rotary switch
absolute
Such switches exist, but I have not checked a small panel-mount one with a thumb-wheel mount, so it is not recommended yet.
Proposal: option 2 for v0.1 (two switches and a cam, absolute, nothing to buy), with option 3 kept for a later volume or fine control.
